sessions.title: Connect quantity to gender and noun case

steps.title: One agrees with its noun
steps.body: один мальчик — one boy. одна девушка — one girl. The numeral meaning one agrees with its noun in gender, number and case. These displayed counting phrases use a singular noun: the masculine boy takes the masculine numeral, and the feminine girl takes the feminine numeral. The guided choice asks for another phrase with one, not the same noun.

steps.title: The scope of the counting rule
steps.body: For nominative counting phrases, one takes a singular noun, two through four take a genitive singular noun, and five through twenty take a genitive plural noun. Apply this shortcut to an accusative phrase only where its forms coincide with the nominative. Animate accusative phrases and other cases need their own case forms; the shortcut is not a rule that all number phrases keep these endings.

steps.title: Two, three and four form a group
steps.body: две девушки — two girls. три кошки — three cats. Both displayed nouns are genitive singular after these numerals, although the quantity is greater than one and these endings can resemble nominative plural. The numeral for two has a feminine form; the form for three does not change for the noun gender. The check asks for another example in the two-through-four group, not an English translation of the cue.

steps.title: Five and higher in the displayed group
steps.body: пять девушек — five girls. десять копеек — ten kopeks. Here the nouns are genitive plural. Five and ten belong to the same noun-form group; one and two do not. Numbers whose last two digits are 11 through 14 also use this group, including 111 through 114. These choices recognize supplied number phrases; they do not test independently producing every noun ending.

sessions.title: Distinguish dative, instrumental and prepositional numeral forms

steps.title: A changed form can name a different case
steps.body: двум — Дательный, the dative. двумя — Творительный, the instrumental. Both are declined forms of the numeral meaning two. Dative commonly marks a recipient or goal; instrumental can mark accompaniment or means. The final part of the form distinguishes these two shown examples; it is not enough to recognize the quantity two.

steps.title: Read a row in its case context
steps.body: Дательный means dative; Творительный means instrumental; Предложный means prepositional. A form must be interpreted with its construction. The bare form двух can occur in more than one case. The admitted row includes the preposition and is labelled prepositional; the check does not claim that a bare ending always uniquely identifies a case. In oblique number phrases the plural noun normally carries the case required by the construction.

steps.title: The displayed prepositional row
steps.body: (о) двух / (об) обоих / (о) полутора — Предложный. This complete row gives the prepositional forms for two, both and one and a half. The parentheses show the accompanying preposition; it is not part of the numeral itself. The prepositional choice contrasts with the dative двум and instrumental двумя. Recognizing this row does not demonstrate independently declining a complete number phrase.

sessions.title: Connect both to gender and case

steps.title: Dative both has two gender forms
steps.body: обеим — Дательный. обоим — Дательный. Both forms mean both in the dative. The feminine series has the stem seen in обеим; the masculine/neuter series has the stem seen in обоим. Gender refers to the counted noun. Changing the gender series does not change the case: both displayed forms are dative.

steps.title: Meaning, gender and the dative row
steps.body: Both refers to the full pair, rather than an unspecified quantity of two. The retained nominative table distinguishes masculine/neuter and feminine forms. The dative row двум / обеим / полутора places two, feminine both and one and a half together by case, not by equal meaning. sessions.title: Distinguish cardinal, ordinal and collective number forms

steps.title: Two and three as collective quantities
steps.body: два — дво́е. три — тро́е. A cardinal states a quantity; a collective presents that quantity as a group. An ordinal states position in a sequence. Thus дво́е is the collective for two, and тро́е is the collective for three. The option второ́й means second, and тре́тий means third; these are ordinal positions, not collective quantities.

steps.title: Collectives have restricted uses
steps.body: Collective number forms are not a general replacement for cardinal numbers with every noun. Standard uses include groups of male people, children or people expressed by appropriate group nouns, personal pronouns, and certain nouns used only in the plural. Use ordinary cardinals with female-person nouns in standard usage; do not infer that any feminine noun takes a collective. This lesson explains the restriction without introducing new Russian noun combinations.

sessions.title: Read decade ranges in their century context

steps.title: A decade is a range of years
steps.body: В шестидесятых годах — in the 1960s. В девяностых годах — in the 1990s. These expressions refer to decade ranges rather than a single year. The ordinal describing the decade and the noun meaning years are in the prepositional plural. The two displayed choices distinguish the sixties from the nineties.

steps.title: The century comes from context
steps.body: Here the supplied English glosses assume the twentieth century. A decade expression by itself does not fix the century in every context; an explicit century or the surrounding discussion can identify it. Read the decade word, not just the shared ending for years. sessions.title: Locate the beginning, middle or end of a period

steps.title: The end of a year and the beginning of a century
steps.body: В конце года — at the end of the year. В начале века — at the beginning of the century. The position word identifies which part of the period is meant, while the following noun identifies the period. Both parts matter: an end is not a beginning, and a year is not a century.

steps.title: The two nouns have different case roles
steps.body: In these expressions, the location noun after the preposition is prepositional, and the noun naming the period is genitive. The English of relationship links the part to the larger period. Do not assign one case to both nouns simply because they appear in the same time phrase.

steps.title: The middle of the week
steps.body: В середине недели — in the middle of the week. This locates an event within the central part of a week; it does not mean the end of a year or the beginning of a century. The checks match complete supplied expressions, not independently produced period-and-position combinations.

sessions.title: Place one action during another event

steps.title: An event supplies the time frame
steps.body: Она родилась во время войны. — She was born during the war. Во время поездки я познакомился с новыми друзьями. — During the trip I met new friends. The war and trip are the surrounding events during which the birth and meeting happen. During does not mean that the birth or meeting continued for the entire war or trip.

steps.title: Meaning and case of the surrounding event
steps.body: The compound preposition meaning during takes the event noun in the genitive. Match the whole sentence: birth during a war differs from meeting friends during a trip. This expresses when an event happens within another event, not the time needed to complete a task. The supplied translations do not demonstrate constructing every during-an-event sentence.

sessions.title: Read the interval over which activity occurs

steps.title: A lesson and a day as intervals
steps.body: В течение урока ученики работали над проектом. — Throughout the lesson, the students worked on the project. В течение дня погода менялась несколько раз. — During the course of the day, the weather changed several times. The interval contains the activity or repeated events. Project work over the lesson does not by itself assert that the project was finished.

steps.body: It emphasizes the duration over which something occurs. The compound preposition takes a genitive noun naming the interval. The weather example explicitly describes several changes during the day, so the expression need not mean one continuous unchanged action. Compare the whole proposition as well as the interval: students and a project differ from weather changes. These checks identify supplied meanings, not task-completion time.

sessions.title: Distinguish before, after, in a period and ago

steps.title: Before and after a reference event
steps.body: Перед ужином мы ходили в парк. — before. После работы я смотрела фильм. — after. The first places the park visit earlier than dinner; the second places watching a film later than work. The preposition meaning before takes an instrumental noun; the one meaning after takes a genitive noun. The English labels classify only this time relation, not the full sentence translation.

steps.title: A time point is different from a duration
steps.body: The future-looking in expression locates an event after an interval from the reference time. Ago locates an event before the reference time. Neither meaning alone states how long the activity lasts or how long it takes to finish a task. Before and after a named event likewise express order relative to that event, not completion.

steps.title: The forward and backward interval examples
steps.body: Мы едем в Латвию через год. — in (a period of time). Мы ездили в Казахстан год назад. — ago. In the first sentence the planned Latvia journey is a year after the reference time; in the second the Kazakhstan journey was a year before it. The forward-looking time construction takes accusative, not genitive; the time noun here has the same surface form as nominative. Ago follows an accusative time expression. The choices classify the shown time relation, not independently produce the whole sentence.

sessions.title: Distinguish time spent from completion within a period

steps.title: Time spent does not assert the task was finished
steps.body: An imperfective verb with a bare accusative time expression states time spent on an activity and does not assert completion. Анна читала статью два часа. — time spent reading without asserting completion. Борис писал письмо час. — time spent writing without asserting completion. These report time devoted to reading or writing. Not asserting completion does not mean asserting that the task was never finished.

steps.title: The completed task and its time frame
steps.body: A perfective verb with an accusative time expression after the preposition states the period within which a bounded task was completed. Анна прочитала статью за два часа. — the article was finished within two hours. Here the perfective reading verb and the completion-time construction present the article as finished within the two-hour period. Contrast that with time spent reading without asserting completion. This completion interval differs from the forward-looking time until the Latvia journey. The current choices classify three supplied sentences; they do not test independently choosing aspect and constructing a time phrase.

sessions.title: Distinguish a negative verb from a negative noun predicate

steps.title: A speaking reply and its negative
steps.body: Да, говорю́ — Yes, I'm speaking. Нет, не говорю́ — No, I'm not speaking. The first word of each reply answers yes or no. The separate negative particle before the speaking verb negates that predicate; it is not merely the initial no reply. The guided choice keeps the speaking action and changes it to a negative reply.

steps.title: A verb and a zero present copula
steps.body: To negate a verb, simply add не (nye) before the verb: the shown examples illustrate this ordinary predicate-negation pattern. In a present-tense noun predicate, the verb corresponding to is is normally omitted. The negative particle can then stand before the noun predicate itself. That is a different structure from a speaking verb with a negative particle.

steps.title: The question and the student statement
steps.body: Вы говори́те? — Are you speaking? Он не студент — He's not a student. The speaking question is not itself negated. The student statement has a noun predicate and no overt present-tense is. The check asks for that negative nominal sentence, not another speaking reply.

steps.title: A complete negative coming sentence
steps.body: Борис не приходит — Boris isn't coming. The negative particle precedes the coming verb. This complete sentence identifies Boris as the subject and coming as the action. The options не студент and не говорю́ are shorter fragments about being a student or speaking; they do not express the complete Boris-coming sentence. These choices recognize supplied structures rather than independently constructing every negative predicate.

steps.body:
Да, говорю́ — Yes, I'm speaking. Нет, не говорю́ — No, I'm not speaking. The first word of each reply answers yes or no. The separate negative particle before the speaking verb negates that predicate; it is not merely the initial no reply. The guided choice keeps the speaking action and changes it to a negative reply.

To negate a verb, simply add не (nye) before the verb: the shown examples illustrate this ordinary predicate-negation pattern. In a present-tense noun predicate, the verb corresponding to is is normally omitted. The negative particle can then stand before the noun predicate itself. That is a different structure from a speaking verb with a negative particle.

Вы говори́те? — Are you speaking? Он не студент — He's not a student. The speaking question is not itself negated. The student statement has a noun predicate and no overt present-tense is. The check asks for that negative nominal sentence, not another speaking reply.

Борис не приходит — Boris isn't coming. The negative particle precedes the coming verb. This complete sentence identifies Boris as the subject and coming as the action. The options не студент and не говорю́ are shorter fragments about being a student or speaking; they do not express the complete Boris-coming sentence. These choices recognize supplied structures rather than independently constructing every negative predicate.

sessions.title: Distinguish negative pronouns from absence and indefinite forms

steps.title: Nobody and nothing refer to different categories
steps.body: кто — никто́. что — ничто́. The first pair concerns a person and nobody; the second concerns a thing and nothing. The indefinite options не́кто and не́что refer to an unspecified person or thing, not the corresponding nobody/nothing form. Do not treat a similar-looking prefix as proof of the same meaning.

steps.title: No person available for an action
steps.body: Negative predicative constructions express the absence of a person or thing for an action. The construction selects a case form; it has no nominative form. Compare the indefinite pronoun separately. не́кого спросить — there is nobody to ask. This is absence of a person available for the infinitive action; it differs from an unspecified person and from there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The case comes from the construction
steps.body: не́кто is an indefinite pronoun, a person whose identity is not specified. It is not the predicative negative of кто. Absence of a person uses a case form: не́кого has the same form in the genitive and accusative, while не́кому is dative and не́кем instrumental. The sentence determines the case; absence meaning alone does not. There is no nominative form in this negative paradigm. The current checks recognize the absence meaning; they do not uniquely identify genitive from the shared genitive/accusative form.

sessions.title: Interpret the supplied readings in stated contexts

steps.title: Two supplied readings with their stated contexts
steps.body: Не надо меня уговаривать. — One should not persuade me in the supplied context where the speaker would never agree. Меня не надо уговаривать. — There is no need to persuade me in the supplied context where the speaker will do it anyway. steps.title: Word order is not a universal meaning switch
steps.body: Word order can change what is in focus or in the scope of a particle. It does not by itself assign one unique meaning to every sentence. Intonation and discourse context matter as well. The current source illustrates these two contextual readings; a speaker could use a sentence with a different intended emphasis in another context. The checks recognize the supplied reading, not a universal rule that moving the subject always changes prohibition into lack of necessity.

sessions.title: Distinguish negating the state from negating its experiencer

steps.title: Not cold and not me are different scopes
steps.body: Мне не холодно. — To me it is not cold. This can also be expressed in English as I am not cold. Не мне холодно. — It is not to me that it is cold. The first negates the cold state for the experiencer; the second contrasts the experiencer, so the person who is cold is not me. The second does not by itself identify that other person.

The check asks for the scope shown in this pair, not free production of every negative-focus construction.

sessions.title: Distinguish the parts of a Russian personal name

steps.title: First name, patronymic and family name
steps.body: имя means first name. отчество means patronymic name. фамилия means family name. A patronymic identifies the father-derived part of a name; it is not the family name. These labels identify three name components rather than three alternative words for the same component.

steps.title: A suffix is not a whole name category
steps.body: The retained introductory pattern describes a father's first name with ович, meaning son of, or овна, meaning daughter of. These are suffix labels, not whole words meaning first name, patronymic name or family name. They illustrate common patronymic patterns; they are not an exhaustive formation rule for every name.

sessions.title: Distinguish a request, thanks and an apology

steps.title: Request and thanks have different functions
steps.body: Пожа́луйста means please in the supplied request use. Спаси́бо means thanks or thank you. A request asks for something; thanks responds with gratitude. The checks use these functions rather than treating all courtesy words as interchangeable.

steps.title: An apology is not thanks
steps.body: Извини́те means excuse me with polite or plural address. Извини́ is the familiar singular form. In the checked descriptions, excuse me, polite or plural identifies the first form; excuse me, familiar singular identifies the second. Neither is the thank you response.

steps.title: Read the address distinction
steps.body: The ending in Извини́те permits polite address to one person or address to more than one person. It does not mean that every use has several listeners. The checked contrast identifies the supplied form, not a rule that a familiar apology is suitable for every relationship. The pronunciation label Pozhalusta in the older source is not another English meaning of please.

sessions.title: Recognize a name question and the start of its reply

steps.title: Ask for a name
steps.body: Как Вас зову́т? means What is your name? This supplied formula uses polite or plural address. The capital letter is a written courtesy convention; it does not create a different spoken pronoun. The question asks for a name rather than for an apology or a general report of how someone is doing.

steps.title: Begin the reply and then give the name
steps.body: Меня́ зову́т means My name is... It starts the name reply and must be followed by a name to give the requested information. The check recognizes that reply opening; it does not treat the fragment alone as a completed personal introduction.

steps.title: Distinguish the other conversational functions
steps.body: Прошу́ проще́ния means I'm sorry / excuse me (formal), an apology. Как дела́? means How are you?, another question. Neither supplies the name requested by Как Вас зову́т? The matching reply opening is Меня́ зову́т. Use the conversational function of each formula rather than choosing another question.

sessions.title: Classify the documented name forms and their stated coloring

steps.title: Explain the Russian classification labels
steps.body: Марюня is classified here as от полной формы имени, meaning from the full form of the name. Машенька is classified as от краткой формы, meaning from the short form. The retained examples relate these to Мария and Маша respectively. These are documented examples, not a rule for generating a derivative from any full or short name.

steps.title: Distinguish derivation from social coloring
steps.body: Сашка is classified in this material as оттенок пренебрежения, meaning a shade of dismissiveness. That label describes social coloring; the two labels about full and short forms describe derivational bases. A form can have a base and social coloring at the same time. The question asks for the classification documented for this example, not mutually exclusive properties of every name.

steps.title: Keep the coloring claim within its context
steps.body: The retained text associates diminutive forms with the suffix -к- with dismissive coloring. Treat this as the source's classification of its examples, not proof that every use of every such name is insulting. Relationship, tone and setting affect interpretation. A documented label does not authorize inventing a new personal-name form or addressing someone that way without regard to their preference.

sessions.title: Interpret supplied word order in context

steps.title: Separate the event from the focus
steps.body: В магазин пошёл я. can emphasize the traveler in the supplied context: It was me who went to the shop. Here someone wrongly attributes the trip to another person and the speaker corrects that attribution. The event is still the speaker going to the shop. “The speaker did not go to the shop.” negates that event; “The speaker went somewhere other than the shop.” changes its destination. Those readings do not fit this affirmative sentence and stated context. The older label To the shop went I merely imitates the Russian arrangement in English; it is not the best natural paraphrase of its communicative focus.

steps.title: Read a story opening in its stated context
steps.body: Пошёл я в магазин. is used here at the beginning of a story about a past visit. “I went to the shop, and the story continues.” expresses that supplied narrative reading. “I did not go to the shop.” negates the event. “I will go to the shop after deciding to leave.” changes it to a future decision, which is not the stated past-story context. The retained source also gives a decision reading in a different context; this question does not infer one universal interpretation from the arrangement alone. Went I to the shop is the older literal arrangement label, not normal neutral English narration.

steps.title: Recognize a neutral report without inventing a contrast
steps.body: Я пошёл в магазин. is used here to report a past trip without contrasting the traveler or destination. “I went to the shop.” expresses that reading. “It was someone else, not me, who went to the shop.” changes the traveler; “I did not go to the shop.” changes the affirmation to negation. All three supplied Russian shop sentences describe the same basic speaker-and-shop event. Their use can differ with focus, intonation and discourse context; word order alone does not guarantee a unique English paraphrase in every situation.

steps.title: New and known information require context
steps.body: В ко́мнату вбежа́л ма́льчик — Into the room rushed a boy. Ма́льчик вбежа́л в ко́мнату — The boy rushed into the room. These retained examples illustrate an introduced boy versus a boy treated as known in their supplied readings. Russian does not add an English article by moving a noun. The English a/the choice also depends on context and what the listener already knows. The shop checks identify supplied contextual readings, not a rule that every reordered sentence changes who acted or where they went.

sessions.title: Recognize written letter case and its address limits

steps.title: Recognize the initial letter before interpreting the addressee
steps.body: The supplied forms Вы, Вас and Вам each begin with a capital letter. The answer capital letter describes that visible initial. Minuscule means a lowercase letter; the option minuscule does not describe these displayed initials. The option plural form describes grammatical shape, not letter case. These are recognition checks, not a test of how many people a sentence addresses.

steps.title: Distinguish polite singular address from grammatical plural shape
steps.body: The retained grammar note describes polite address to one person using forms shared with the plural. In personal letters and official papers, a capital initial can mark respectful address to one recipient. This written convention is different from plural meaning. The same grammatical forms can address several people, so a capital initial alone does not establish the number of addressees. Identify the recipient from context, not from the English label plural form.

steps.title: Keep capitalization tied to written context
steps.body: In the supplied respectful written-address convention, Вы, Вас and Вам have capital initials. Current Gramota guidance distinguishes respectful address to one recipient from address to several people or a general audience, where lowercase is used. A sentence-initial capital is also ordinary sentence capitalization and need not mark respectful singular address. Lowercase outside this convention is not automatically rude. Capitalization cannot be heard in speech. These checks recognize the shown letter case; choosing forms for a new letter requires recipient and genre context.

sessions.title: Distinguish locality, street, building and apartment marks

steps.title: Recognize the locality mark
steps.body: In 115114 г. Москва, г. marks the city or locality; the supplied English gloss is city. The number is a postcode, not the abbreviation being tested. The options street and building refer to different components. Read the requested abbreviation rather than treating every number or place name as the same part of an address.

steps.title: Distinguish street, building and apartment
steps.body: In ул. Петрова, д. 14, кв. 15, the first mark ул. identifies the street. The later д. identifies the building, and кв. identifies the apartment. The supplied line thus separates street name, building number and apartment number. The answer street matches the first mark; city belongs to the locality mark and apartment belongs to the later mark. Abbreviations label address components; their positions and associated numbers help distinguish them.

steps.title: Identify a building mark without inventing delivery details

sessions.title: Distinguish specific unknown, open and speaker-known reference

steps.title: A specific person whose identity is unknown
steps.body: В доме действительно кто-то был means that someone really was in the house. The label референтность и неизвестность говорящему describes reference to a particular person whose identity is unknown to the speaker in this supplied use. It does not mean nobody was there. Referential concerns whether a particular entity is intended; it is different from whether the speaker knows that entity's identity.

steps.title: An unspecified alternative is not absence
steps.body: куда-нибудь is the supplied example of an open, unspecified destination. The label являются нереферентными means non-referential in this classification: no particular fixed destination is selected. An alternative is considered against other possible destinations, as in a future plan, desire or conditional context. This is not the label референтность и неизвестность говорящему for a particular unknown entity, nor референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости for a specific entity known to the speaker. The classification concerns this supplied series/use, not a universal translation of every indefinite form.

steps.title: A specific choice known to the speaker, with overlap limits
steps.body: кое-какие is classified as референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости: weakly definite reference to particular things known to the speaker but not assumed known to the listener. It differs from a particular unknown entity and from an open alternative with no fixed referent. The retained rule Местоимение на -то может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на -нибудь says the first series can also be used with the meaning of the second in some contexts. Do not infer a rigid one-suffix/one-meaning division. These checks classify the supplied forms; broader production and selection need the sentence and discourse context.

sessions.title: Apply a supplied letter framework without universal style rules

steps.title: Organize the supplied problem-and-request letter
steps.body: In this lesson's problem-and-request model, state the reason, explain relevant facts, then make the request. For a letter explaining a problem and requesting action, this sequence gives the recipient a reason and relevant support for the request. It is a supplied framework, not a rule that every Russian letter must put its main point last. English and Russian letters have different genres and purposes; a source's contrast is not a universal rule for either language.

steps.title: Distinguish the greeting, body and closing
steps.body: Здравствуйте! is a greeting, not a rule about how close the recipient is. The retained example glosses it as Greetings. Уважаемый Иван Иванович is another supplied address formula, glossed Respected Ivan Ivanovich. Select address wording for the recipient, relationship and genre; the English word dear is not a universal ban determined by this neutral greeting. The claim every unfamiliar recipient forbids any greeting translated as dear overgeneralizes from one greeting to every addressee. In the supplied layout, Sender’s address and date precedes the Greeting, then comes the Body, followed by Closing and signature. A greeting starts the address to the reader; the body carries the message; the closing and signature end the letter. The framework is not mandatory for every letter or electronic message.

steps.title: Read what happened to the described entity
steps.body: A past passive participle describes an entity affected by an action. The supplied form сде́ланный has the meaning done/made. The form напи́санный means written, and уби́тый means killed. These words describe what was done to the entity; they do not identify it as the person doing the action. The three supplied meanings differ by the underlying action. Choosing written for сде́ланный would replace doing or making with writing; choosing killed would replace it with killing.

steps.title: Recognize the supplied long forms without inventing a universal algorithm
steps.body: The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. Broader formation includes other suffix patterns and lexical restrictions, so do not manufacture an unlisted form from this small set. An imperfective past passive can exist; the supplied perfective examples are not a universal claim that every past passive must come from a perfective verb.

steps.title: Distinguish the action meaning from long versus short form
steps.body: The meaning written belongs to напи́санный, not to the doing/making form сде́ланный or the killing form уби́тый. The meaning killed belongs to уби́тый, not to the other two actions. The retained short form напи́сан has a single n and lacks the long adjective ending shown in напи́санный. Long versus short form is different from the action meaning: both writing forms concern writing. These checks select the action meaning of a supplied form; they do not test production of all short-form gender and number endings.

steps.title: Identify the writer in the retained passive sentence
steps.body: письмо написано Иваном — the letter was written by Ivan. The letter is the entity affected by the writing; Ivan is the writer identified in the retained sentence. The passive form describes the letter’s state or result, rather than saying that the letter writes somebody. The short passive form in the sentence differs from the long headword напи́санный. A longer sentence supplies context that a headword lacks; do not infer a writer, reader or exact time from a bare participle alone. Active participles are outside this required Unit27 lesson.

steps.title: Meaning differs between a passive description, a finite verb and an infinitive
steps.body: The supplied обсужда́емый has the meaning being discussed. It describes something affected by discussion, rather than naming the person doing the discussing. The source also permits an able-to-be-discussed reading; the checked English option here is being discussed. The supporting verb form оставля́ем means we leave: it is a first-person plural present-tense form, with we performing the action, not a passive description. The infinitive оставля́ть means to leave and does not by itself name a we subject. Choose we leave for the finite form and to leave for the infinitive. The option to discuss is an infinitive meaning rather than the checked passive description. Different action meanings and grammatical functions must not be exchanged simply because forms share a stem.

sessions.title: Read the described letter, writer and separate main action

steps.title: Separate the letter description from the sentence action
steps.body: Письмо, написанное Анной, лежит на столе. means the letter Anna wrote is on the table. The participial phrase написанное Анной describes the letter: written is the action affecting it, and Anna is the named writer. The main statement locates the letter on the table. Being written and being on the table are separate parts of the reading. Neither the table nor the letter is the writer. The sentence does not say that Anna put the letter away, and the writer is not identified as its reader. A passive participle describes the affected entity; an agent phrase can name the person responsible for that particular action.

steps.title: Do not transfer the main-action subject to an unnamed participle agent
steps.body: Анна убрала прочитанное письмо. means Anna put away the letter that had been read. Anna performs the putting-away action; the description прочитанное письмо says that the letter had already been read. The sentence does not name the reader. Anna might or might not have read it; neither reading can be asserted from this sentence alone. Already read is different from just written or still reading aloud. The supplied passive description expresses the completed reading of the letter, not an ongoing action by Anna. Recognize the main verb, the affected letter and any explicitly named agent separately. These checks interpret the supplied readings; accent placement alone cannot answer who wrote or read the letter, and recognizing these examples does not demonstrate production of an unfamiliar participial sentence.

steps.body:
Письмо, написанное Анной, лежит на столе. means the letter Anna wrote is on the table. The sentence does not say that Anna put the letter away, and the writer is not identified as its reader. A passive participle describes the affected entity; an agent phrase can name the person responsible for that particular action.

Анна убрала прочитанное письмо. means Anna put away the letter that had been read. Anna performs the putting-away action; the description прочитанное письмо says that the letter had already been read. The sentence does not name the reader. The supplied passive description expresses the completed reading of the letter, not an ongoing action by Anna. Recognize the main verb, the affected letter and any explicitly named agent separately. steps.title: Read two actions happening together
steps.body: An imperfective verbal adverb describes an accompanying action. In the supplied читая письмо, он улыбался, he was reading the letter while he smiled. Reading and smiling overlap: simultaneous means during the same interval as the main predicate. The main verb places this example in the past; читая does not independently mean absolute present time. The retained examples думая and учась illustrate imperfective verbal-adverb forms. An isolated form cannot establish the tense of an absent main verb.

steps.title: Keep the two actions with the same person
steps.body: In читая письмо, он улыбался, The pronoun he is the explicit main-clause subject. The reader and the person smiling are the same person. Identify the main verb and its subject before deciding who performs the accompanying action. The retained label выделяется запятыми с двух сторон names that treatment. A single comma before the phrase would omit its closing boundary in this supplied sentence.

steps.title: Compare the phrase placed before its noun
steps.body: In Написанная в спешке программа выполнила недопустимую операцию. The same descriptive phrase precedes the noun. The supplied example has no separating commas: запятые не ставятся is its label. Phrase position helps distinguish these two examples; this does not mean commas are never used before a described noun.

steps.title: Apply the pronoun and cause exceptions
steps.body: The retained rule states exceptions when the described entity is a personal pronoun or the participial phrase expresses a cause. Воспитанный в традициях Фоппы, Бернардо Дзенале и Амброджо Бергоньоне, он прошёл обучение в мастерской Леонардо. The opening phrase describes он, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The comma after Фоппы is internal to the list of names. The later comma after Бергоньоне marks the modifier boundary before он; do not treat every visible comma as a modifier boundary. Изумлённый этим хохотом, Павел сел на пол и смотрел куда-то в угол The retained source row explicitly gives this example a causal shade, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The ordinary preceding-noun label запятые не ставятся cannot cancel these exceptions. The optional source wording личным местоимением and кроме тех случаев identifies a category/connective, not a complete comma decision; its reference question does not satisfy these language checks.

steps.title: Check the continuing clause and sentence end
steps.body: Туча, нависшая над высокими вершинами тополей, уже сыпала дождиком The phrase describes Туча and is followed by the continuing predicate, so Separating commas mark both boundaries of the participial phrase before the sentence continues. Вдали виднеется маяк, стоящий у моря Here the phrase describes маяк and ends the supplied construction, so A separating comma precedes the terminal participial phrase, with no closing comma at sentence end. A closing separating comma would have no continuing clause after it. By contrast, No separating comma is used between the participial phrase and the word it describes. is the ordinary non-causal, non-pronoun preceding-noun default shown in the earlier program example. These are bounded supplied constructions; not every phrase before a noun needs a comma and not every phrase after a word fits one universal rule.

sessions.title: In this admitted pair, the adverbial opening is the bookish option and the finite coordination is the ordinary option.

steps.title: Contrast the adverbial opening with finite coordination
steps.body: In Закончив письмо, Анна пошла на почту., finishing the letter is expressed by the opening verbal adverb. In Анна закончила письмо и пошла на почту., the actions are expressed by coordinated finite verbs. The adverbial opening is the bookish option and the finite coordination the ordinary option in this admitted pair. Both describe finishing before going to the post office; the register choice does not reverse those events.

steps.title: Keep the register claim inside this particular pair
steps.body: The supplied Написанное письмо лежит на столе. contains a passive description and is outside this adverbial-versus-finite pair. Mere appearance in writing also does not establish this bookish classification. A verbal adverb in a different sentence needs its own contextual evidence: this pair does not license every adverbial as bookish. Recognizing the opening word is different from interpreting the whole sentence or judging an unfamiliar style.

sessions.title: Read the passage for the actions, not for whether the style is bookish.

steps.title: Follow the actor and the order of actions
steps.body: In Закончив письмо, Анна пошла на почту и отправила его., Anna finishes the letter before going to the post office and sending it. Anna performs the actions; the letter does not travel alone and the post office does not write it. The finishing phrase belongs before the departure, not after the sending. Read the entire supplied passage when a check shows only a fragment.

steps.title: Resolve the final action without substituting a register answer
steps.body: The supplied отправила его means she sent it, with the letter as the object in this passage. The passage places the sending after Anna goes to the post office. It does not say that she stayed at the table, finished at the market, left the letter at home or received a letter at home. Those alternatives replace a stated event or location. Bookish register classification is a separate objective and cannot answer who acted, where she went or what she did with the letter.

sessions.title: Answer from the admitted capstone story

steps.title: Follow the rescue before the second return
steps.body: In the retained story a woman reports that a two-year-old girl remains in the burning house. Bob, the dog sent by the firefighters, returns carrying the girl. The supplied нёс де́вочку belongs to that rescue, before the later discovery involving a doll. The mother is glad her daughter is alive; the passage does not describe the rescue itself as the comic discovery.

steps.title: Connect the laughter to what the dog carries next
steps.body: After the rescue Bob goes back into the house and returns carrying a large doll, expressed by несла́ большу́ю ку́клу. When the people recognize it, все расхохота́лись describes their laughter. The female grammatical form refers to the dog in that part of the narration, not the rescued girl carrying the doll. Match the reaction to the doll discovery and keep the earlier rescue separate. These checks interpret the supplied story, not an unfamiliar passage.

The retained стоять entry is a verb with стоять, стою, стоит, стоял and the sense remaining upright on a base. Ваза стоит на столе. illustrates that standing action. Use the sense field to distinguish стоит from the furniture noun. The label сущ. identifies a part of speech; it does not state the furniture sense. When a check shows only a label or a row of forms, select the stated information limit rather than guessing that it contains a definition. These checks use two supplied entries, not an unrestricted external dictionary or a claim of completed book work.

provenanceRecords.sourceRecordId: future:In English, when reporting a story, we usually change the tense of what was said
provenanceRecords.shippedText: In English, when reporting a story, we usually change the tense of what was said: compare "I ''am'' English" with "He said he ''was'' English" - the reported verb changes tense. In Russian, however, we keep the tense the same, so the same report is literally, "He said he '''is''' English" - "'''Он сказа́л, что он англича́нин'''", not "'''Он сказа́л, что он ''был'' англича́нином'''".

provenanceRecords.sourceRecordId: date-russia:In [[Russia]], dates are usually written in "day month year" (DMY) order. This o
provenanceRecords.shippedText:
In Russia, dates are usually written in "day month year" (DMY) order. This order is used in both the all-numeric date (for example "28.08.17") and the expanded form (for example "28 августа 2017 г."); the trailing "г" is short for "года" (goda, "of the year"). Coincidentally, in Polish the word for year is "rok", so a similar date format is used by the Poles e.g. 1987r). Single-digit numbers for day or month may have a preceding zero (for example "28.08.2017") is more usual.

When saying the date, it is usually pronounced using the ordinal number of the day first (in neutral grammatical gender), then the month in genitive case (for example "Двадцать восьмое августа").

provenanceRecords.shippedText: Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. An apartment or office number is included only when the premises has one, and it is omitted when the premises has none.

In the nominative singular, мо́й is masculine and моя́ is feminine. For стол choose мо́й; for собака choose моя́. The form follows the noun being described.

моё is the neuter singular nominative form of my. мои́ is the plural nominative form. A singular noun does not take the plural form in these choices.

Наш means our; Ваш means your. In the worked phrase на́ша сестра́, both words are feminine singular nominative. Keep the same noun and feminine singular agreement. на́шего бра́та changes the referent, and на́ши is plural.

тво́й is masculine singular nominative; твоя́ is feminine singular nominative. Both mean your. To change the masculine form to the feminine form while keeping nominative singular, choose твоя́.

After ж, ц, ч, ш, or щ, an unstressed о in an ending is written е. That replacement is not a rule for every unstressed о. In хоро́шее, the unstressed ending after ш uses е. The и in хоро́шие follows a different spelling condition: write и rather than ы after ш. Spelling limits the letters in an ending; gender, number and case determine which form is needed.

To put the phrase in the accusative singular, change both words: хоро́шая книга becomes хоро́шую книгу. An adjective agrees with its noun in gender, number and case. In хорошее письмо, the adjective describes a neuter singular noun. хоро́ший is the dictionary form: masculine singular nominative. The following forms belong to the same adjective meaning good.

After ж, ц, ч, ш, or щ, an unstressed о in an ending is written е. That replacement is not a rule for every unstressed о. In хоро́шее, the unstressed ending after ш uses е. The и in хоро́шие follows a different spelling condition: write и rather than ы after ш. Spelling limits the letters in an ending; gender, number and case determine which form is needed.

хоро́шая is feminine singular nominative; хоро́шее is neuter singular nominative. In хоро́шая книга, both words are feminine singular nominative. To put the phrase in the accusative singular, change both words: хоро́шая книга becomes хоро́шую книгу. Keep the same noun and feminine singular agreement. хоро́шего друга is masculine animate; хоро́шие книги is plural.

хоро́шие is plural nominative. To change хоро́шее from neuter singular nominative to plural nominative, choose хоро́шие. To go back to neuter singular, choose хоро́шее. To supply the dictionary form, choose хоро́ший. These choices test the requested form of the adjective; all the options are already correctly spelled.

Adjectives agree with their nouns in gender, number and case. In хорошее письмо, the adjective describes a neuter singular noun. хоро́ший is the dictionary form: masculine singular nominative. This lesson compares singular and plural nominative forms, then explains the spelling in the retained plurals.

After г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, or щ, write и rather than ы. The seven-letter condition is required. This rule applies to the spelling of noun and adjective endings. In кни́ги, и follows г; in хоро́шие, и follows ш. The rule controls spelling, but the question determines the required gender, number and case.

For these nominative checks, кни́га means book in the singular and кни́ги means books in the plural. To form this plural, replace the singular ending with the plural ending: кни́га becomes кни́ги. The stem ends in г, so the seven-letter rule requires и. To return to singular nominative, choose кни́га.

кни́ги is plural nominative in this lesson. дни is also plural nominative and means days. Its и does not follow a letter in the seven-letter set, so дни is not an example of that spelling replacement. Not every plural ending in и comes from the seven-letter rule. Identify number from the requested form and context.

хоро́шее is neuter singular nominative; хоро́шие is plural nominative. To change the neuter singular form to plural nominative, choose хоро́шие; to return to neuter singular, choose хоро́шее. For the masculine singular dictionary form, choose хоро́ший. All these options are correctly spelled: the questions test form recognition rather than choosing between correct and incorrect spellings.

The instrumental case can mark the means used to do something. These checks first teach its forms. сто́л is the dictionary form, meaning table; столо́м is instrumental singular. The word still names a table: the ending marks its grammatical role, not a new vocabulary meaning.

The instrumental singular -ом fits the hard stem of the relevant noun class. Soft stems use their own instrumental ending, so -ом is not universal. Here, keep the stem of сто́л and add -ом to obtain столо́м. Learn the stress with the whole form.

столу́ is dative singular and столе́ is prepositional singular. Both belong to the same noun, but neither has the instrumental singular ending. For an instrumental singular request, select столо́м rather than selecting a form merely because its English gloss is table.

до́м means house in its dictionary form. до́мом is instrumental singular: keep the stem and add -ом. Given до́м and an instrumental singular request, choose до́мом. This is the same ending pattern as the table form.

до́му is dative singular; до́ме is prepositional singular. They do not answer an instrumental singular request. Compare the entire ending with до́мом, and notice that this noun keeps its stem stress.

поездом is instrumental singular of the noun meaning train; карандашом is instrumental singular of the noun meaning pencil. The pencil check asks for that meaning as well as the case. Its other options refer to train and husband. A correct case alone does not identify the requested noun.

книгой is the instrumental singular form for book. This noun has a different ending from the -ом shown for table and house. Do not attach the same ending to every noun. These examples introduce selected singular patterns, not the full instrumental paradigm.

сорок один год — forty-one years. The compound ends in 1, so its noun follows the one pattern. In basic nominative or inanimate accusative counts, endings 2, 3 or 4 follow the two pattern; endings 0 and 5 through 9 follow the five pattern. Endings 11 through 14 are exceptions to the final-digit rule and take the five pattern. Other grammatical cases need additional changes.

For a five-year row, choose пять лет, rather than два года, which names two years. For a one-year row, choose один год; for a two-year row, choose два года. The separately shown cue can have a different count. These checks recognize quantities of years, not ordinal calendar-year dates or a complete age sentence.

четверть восьмого — 7:15. The eighth hour is the period leading up to eight, not the period starting at eight. A quarter of that hour has elapsed after seven. The ordinal names the next hour and appears in genitive form.

полвосьмого — 7:30. Half of the eighth hour has passed, so the clock shows half past seven. The compact half-hour expression is written as one word in this retained form. Match the construction to the clock reading, rather than treating the named eighth hour as the elapsed whole hour.

без четверти восемь — 7:45. This construction counts a quarter hour remaining until eight: subtract fifteen minutes from the named upcoming hour. The without construction differs from counting a quarter or a half already elapsed. These choices interpret existing forms; context is still needed to distinguish morning from evening.

A current-time question and the time when an event happens are different requests. The retained event sentences use at-time expressions. A preposition introduces several of them, while the without construction expresses minutes remaining until the upcoming hour. Study the complete source examples before selecting their readings.

Концерт начинается в шесть часов. — 18.00. Она была дома в час. — 13.00. These are the readings assigned by the retained source. The bare six-hour and one-hour expressions do not themselves distinguish evening from morning; the source readings depend on context. Do not infer that every occurrence of six means eighteen.

Я приду в четверть восьмого. — 7.15 – quarter of the eighth hour. Он нам позвонил в пятнадцать минут десятого. — 9.15 – 15 minutes of the tenth hour. A quarter or fifteen minutes has elapsed in the hour leading to the named next hour. The ordinal is genitive; the event-time phrase also has its introductory preposition.

Наш рейс уезжает в половине пятого. — 4.30 – half of the fifth hour. Мы будем свободны в полвторого. — 1.30 – half of the second hour. Both name a half elapsed in the next ordinal hour. Their retained preposition and noun forms differ; recognize each complete construction rather than exchanging endings mechanically.

Retained Wikipedia motion table and examples, and Wiktionary dolzhen revision84965088. Cornell Beginning Russian Grammar https://russian.cornell.edu/grammar/html/gr12_b_a.htm le57_62_a.htm (directionality), le57_62_b.htm (setting out), and subject index consulted2026-10-11. Independent English synthesis; linguistic review pending.
отговорить — to dissuade. договориться — to agree. These are different meanings, even though the words share material with a verb of speaking. A prefix is not always just an aspect marker: learn the whole verb and its meaning.

отговаривать is the imperfective partner of perfective отговорить: both concern dissuading. The retained source explicitly identifies this pair. сказать belongs to a separate speaking pair; it is not the imperfective partner of отговорить. For a question asking for the perfective partner of отговаривать, select отговорить. договориться is a different verb meaning to agree.

написать — to write. сделать — to do. Neither expresses dissuading or agreeing. When a question asks for a meaning, translate the displayed verb. When it asks for an aspect partner, preserve the lexical meaning while changing aspect. These selections do not demonstrate creating new prefixed verbs or using aspect in a sentence.

чтобы — so that. если — if. The first conjunction can introduce a purpose; the second introduces a condition. In a purpose construction with the same subject for both actions, an infinitive after the purpose conjunction can name the intended action. This rule is explained here, but the current choices do not require composing such a sentence.

чтобы is an ordinary purpose conjunction. The bookish or archaic qualifier in the retained source belongs to дабы, not to чтобы. The English meaning so that differs from the conditional if and the causal because. Select the meaning of the displayed conjunction; do not infer an archaic register for the ordinary form.

потому что — because. хотя — although. The first gives a reason; the second introduces a concession. The English label after names a temporal relationship rather than a reason. English since can also express a reason, so it is not a contrasting wrong answer to because in this exercise. The causal check instead contrasts because with although and after. These conjunction meanings are distinct from purpose and condition.

тридцать три рюмки — thirty-three shot glasses. сорок один год — forty-one years. In these nominative counting phrases, 33 ends in three and takes a genitive singular noun; 41 ends in one and takes a singular noun. The choice may ask for a different final-digit group from the displayed reference phrase. Read the requested group in the question.

For these whole-number counting phrases, check the last two digits before the final digit. Endings 11 through 14 require genitive plural. Otherwise a final one takes singular, final two through four take genitive singular, and final zero or five through nine take genitive plural. For example, 111 differs from 41; 113 differs from 33. These are numeric rule comparisons, not newly supplied Russian phrases. In other cases the numeral and noun need the relevant declined forms.

шестьдесят девять слов — sixty-nine words. The final nine places 69 in the genitive-plural group. In the three choices, сорок один год ends in one, тридцать три рюмки ends in three, and шестьдесят девять слов ends in nine. Identify the category requested by the question. A displayed 41 phrase does not make the answer to a question about nine a translation or a same-quantity counterpart.

Both refers to the full pair, rather than an unspecified quantity of two. The retained nominative table distinguishes masculine/neuter and feminine forms. The dative row двум / обеим / полутора places two, feminine both and one and a half together by case, not by equal meaning. Дательный is dative, Творительный is instrumental, and Предложный is prepositional.

обеими — Творительный. обоими — Творительный. The feminine and masculine/neuter series remain distinct, but both shown forms are instrumental. Compare обеим with обеими and обоим with обоими: the extra final vowel distinguishes these dative and instrumental examples. два — дво́е. три — тро́е. A cardinal states a quantity; a collective presents that quantity as a group. An ordinal states position in a sequence. Thus дво́е is the collective for two, and тро́е is the collective for three. The option второ́й means second, and тре́тий means third; these are ordinal positions, not collective quantities.

Collective number forms are not a general replacement for cardinal numbers with every noun. Standard uses include groups of male people, children or people expressed by appropriate group nouns, personal pronouns, and certain nouns used only in the plural. Use ordinary cardinals with female-person nouns in standard usage; do not infer that any feminine noun takes a collective. This lesson explains the restriction without introducing new Russian noun combinations.

Thus дво́е is the collective for two, and тро́е is the collective for three. The option второ́й means second, and тре́тий means third; these are ordinal positions, not collective quantities.

Collective number forms are not a general replacement for cardinal numbers with every noun. Standard uses include groups of male people, children or people expressed by appropriate group nouns, personal pronouns, and certain nouns used only in the plural. Use ordinary cardinals with female-person nouns in standard usage; do not infer that any feminine noun takes a collective. This lesson explains the restriction without introducing new Russian noun combinations.

четы́ре — че́тверо. The collective form keeps the quantity four while presenting it as a group. The ordinal distractor четвёртый means fourth, a position; дво́е is a group of two. In the earlier check, че́тверо is a collective but has the wrong quantity for three. Selecting the collective column does not demonstrate choosing its use with every noun or constructing a declined collective phrase.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: Здравствуйте! is a greeting, not a rule about how close the recipient is. The retained example glosses it as Greetings. Уважаемый Иван Иванович is another supplied address formula, glossed Respected Ivan Ivanovich. Select address wording for the recipient, relationship and genre; the English word dear is not a universal ban determined by this neutral greeting. The claim every unfamiliar recipient forbids any greeting translated as dear overgeneralizes from one greeting to every addressee. In the supplied layout, Sender’s address and date precedes the Greeting, then comes the Body, followed by Closing and signature. A greeting starts the address to the reader; the body carries the message; the closing and signature end the letter. The framework is not mandatory for every letter or electronic message.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: В магазин пошёл я. can emphasize the traveler in the supplied context: It was me who went to the shop. Here someone wrongly attributes the trip to another person and the speaker corrects that attribution. The event is still the speaker going to the shop. “The speaker did not go to the shop.” negates that event; “The speaker went somewhere other than the shop.” changes its destination. Those readings do not fit this affirmative sentence and stated context. The older label To the shop went I merely imitates the Russian arrangement in English; it is not the best natural paraphrase of its communicative focus.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: Пошёл я в магазин. is used here at the beginning of a story about a past visit. “I went to the shop, and the story continues.” expresses that supplied narrative reading. “I did not go to the shop.” negates the event. “I will go to the shop after deciding to leave.” changes it to a future decision, which is not the stated past-story context. The retained source also gives a decision reading in a different context; this question does not infer one universal interpretation from the arrangement alone. Went I to the shop is the older literal arrangement label, not normal neutral English narration.

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
В магазин пошёл я. can emphasize the traveler in the supplied context: It was me who went to the shop. Here someone wrongly attributes the trip to another person and the speaker corrects that attribution. The event is still the speaker going to the shop. “The speaker did not go to the shop.” negates that event; “The speaker went somewhere other than the shop.” changes its destination. Those readings do not fit this affirmative sentence and stated context. The older label To the shop went I merely imitates the Russian arrangement in English; it is not the best natural paraphrase of its communicative focus.

Пошёл я в магазин. is used here at the beginning of a story about a past visit. “I went to the shop, and the story continues.” expresses that supplied narrative reading. “I did not go to the shop.” negates the event. “I will go to the shop after deciding to leave.” changes it to a future decision, which is not the stated past-story context. The retained source also gives a decision reading in a different context; this question does not infer one universal interpretation from the arrangement alone. Went I to the shop is the older literal arrangement label, not normal neutral English narration.

Я пошёл в магазин. is used here to report a past trip without contrasting the traveler or destination. “I went to the shop.” expresses that reading. “It was someone else, not me, who went to the shop.” changes the traveler; “I did not go to the shop.” changes the affirmation to negation. All three supplied Russian shop sentences describe the same basic speaker-and-shop event. Their use can differ with focus, intonation and discourse context; word order alone does not guarantee a unique English paraphrase in every situation.

В ко́мнату вбежа́л ма́льчик — Into the room rushed a boy. Ма́льчик вбежа́л в ко́мнату — The boy rushed into the room. These retained examples illustrate an introduced boy versus a boy treated as known in their supplied readings. Russian does not add an English article by moving a noun. The English a/the choice also depends on context and what the listener already knows. The shop checks identify supplied contextual readings, not a rule that every reordered sentence changes who acted or where they went.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: В доме действительно кто-то был means that someone really was in the house. The label референтность и неизвестность говорящему describes reference to a particular person whose identity is unknown to the speaker in this supplied use. It does not mean nobody was there. Referential concerns whether a particular entity is intended; it is different from whether the speaker knows that entity's identity.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: куда-нибудь is the supplied example of an open, unspecified destination. The label являются нереферентными means non-referential in this classification: no particular fixed destination is selected. An alternative is considered against other possible destinations, as in a future plan, desire or conditional context. This is not the label референтность и неизвестность говорящему for a particular unknown entity, nor референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости for a specific entity known to the speaker. The classification concerns this supplied series/use, not a universal translation of every indefinite form.

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
В доме действительно кто-то был means that someone really was in the house. The label референтность и неизвестность говорящему describes reference to a particular person whose identity is unknown to the speaker in this supplied use. It does not mean nobody was there. Referential concerns whether a particular entity is intended; it is different from whether the speaker knows that entity's identity.

куда-нибудь is the supplied example of an open, unspecified destination. The label являются нереферентными means non-referential in this classification: no particular fixed destination is selected. An alternative is considered against other possible destinations, as in a future plan, desire or conditional context. This is not the label референтность и неизвестность говорящему for a particular unknown entity, nor референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости for a specific entity known to the speaker. The classification concerns this supplied series/use, not a universal translation of every indefinite form.

кое-какие is classified as референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости: weakly definite reference to particular things known to the speaker but not assumed known to the listener. It differs from a particular unknown entity and from an open alternative with no fixed referent. The retained rule Местоимение на -то может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на -нибудь says the first series can also be used with the meaning of the second in some contexts. Do not infer a rigid one-suffix/one-meaning division. These checks classify the supplied forms; broader production and selection need the sentence and discourse context.

Distinguish polite singular address from grammatical plural shape

provenanceRecords.shippedText: The retained grammar note describes polite address to one person using forms shared with the plural. In personal letters and official papers, a capital initial can mark respectful address to one recipient. This written convention is different from plural meaning. The same grammatical forms can address several people, so a capital initial alone does not establish the number of addressees. Identify the recipient from context, not from the English label plural form.

In 115114 г. Москва, г. marks the city or locality; the supplied English gloss is city. The number is a postcode, not the abbreviation being tested. The options street and building refer to different components. Read the requested abbreviation rather than treating every number or place name as the same part of an address.

In ул. Петрова, д. 14, кв. 15, the first mark ул. identifies the street. The later д. identifies the building, and кв. identifies the apartment. The supplied line thus separates street name, building number and apartment number. The answer street matches the first mark; city belongs to the locality mark and apartment belongs to the later mark. Abbreviations label address components; their positions and associated numbers help distinguish them.

The separate supplied mark д. has the English gloss building. It does not name the city or street. The line with building and apartment numbers shows why those two numbers must not be confused. These checks recognize marks in retained example lines. They do not prove that a sample address is current or deliverable, prescribe a universal postal order, or require an apartment number where none exists.

The supplied model is Анна Петрова / ул. Садовая, д. 12, кв. 4 / г. Казань / Республика Татарстан / Россия / 420000. It contains a recipient, premises, locality, regional unit, country and postcode. A numeric postal code and a locality perform different roles. The UPU sheet describes a six-digit Russian postcode and illustrates delivery-office coding; a displayed sample code is not a live delivery lookup. A greeting does not replace a recipient name. Recognize each requested component before trying to arrange a whole address.

г. Казань — the locality names the city. The mark and place name identify a locality, not a street or a numeric delivery code. Other labels: The option “the street line names the premises” does not describe the requested component or supplied comparison. The mark and place name identify a locality, not a street or a numeric delivery code.; The option “the postcode names the delivery office” does not describe the requested component or supplied comparison. Анна Петрова — the addressee names the recipient. The personal name identifies who receives the item, not the premises or numeric code. Other labels: The option “the street line names the premises” does not describe the requested component or supplied comparison. The personal name identifies who receives the item, not the premises or numeric code.; The option “the postcode names the delivery office” does not describe the requested component or supplied comparison. The personal name identifies who receives the item, not the premises or numeric code.

ул. Садовая, д. 12, кв. 4 — the street line names the premises. This line contains the street, building and apartment, rather than the recipient or locality. Other labels: The option “the addressee names the recipient” does not describe the requested component or supplied comparison. This line contains the street, building and apartment, rather than the recipient or locality.; The option “the locality names the city” does not describe the requested component or supplied comparison. 420000 — the postcode names the delivery office. The six digits are the numeric postal code, not a person or locality name. Code recognition alone does not verify deliverability. Code recognition alone does not verify deliverability.; The option “the addressee names the recipient” does not describe the requested component or supplied comparison. Здравствуйте — a greeting is outside the address. The greeting belongs to correspondence, not to the recipient-name or postcode component. Республика Татарстан — the republic is the applicable regional unit for this locality. This supplied line names the republic associated with the stated locality, not a numeric code or greeting. Россия — the country names the destination state. This line names the destination country in the supplied model. A postcode serves a different role and does not name the country. In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Recognize the supplied long forms without inventing a universal algorithm

provenanceRecords.shippedText: The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. Broader formation includes other suffix patterns and lexical restrictions, so do not manufacture an unlisted form from this small set. An imperfective past passive can exist; the supplied perfective examples are not a universal claim that every past passive must come from a perfective verb.

Review the complete past-passive distinction

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
A past passive participle describes an entity affected by an action. The supplied form сде́ланный has the meaning done/made. The form напи́санный means written, and уби́тый means killed. These words describe what was done to the entity; they do not identify it as the person doing the action. The three supplied meanings differ by the underlying action. Choosing written for сде́ланный would replace doing or making with writing; choosing killed would replace it with killing.

The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. Broader formation includes other suffix patterns and lexical restrictions, so do not manufacture an unlisted form from this small set. An imperfective past passive can exist; the supplied perfective examples are not a universal claim that every past passive must come from a perfective verb.

The meaning written belongs to напи́санный, not to the doing/making form сде́ланный or the killing form уби́тый. The meaning killed belongs to уби́тый, not to the other two actions. The retained short form напи́сан has a single n and lacks the long adjective ending shown in напи́санный. Long versus short form is different from the action meaning: both writing forms concern writing. These checks select the action meaning of a supplied form; they do not test production of all short-form gender and number endings.

письмо написано Иваном — the letter was written by Ivan. The letter is the entity affected by the writing; Ivan is the writer identified in the retained sentence. The passive form describes the letter’s state or result, rather than saying that the letter writes somebody. The short passive form in the sentence differs from the long headword напи́санный. A longer sentence supplies context that a headword lacks; do not infer a writer, reader or exact time from a bare participle alone. Active participles are outside this required Unit27 lesson.

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
Письмо, написанное Анной, лежит на столе. means the letter Anna wrote is on the table. The participial phrase написанное Анной describes the letter: written is the action affecting it, and Anna is the named writer. The main statement locates the letter on the table. Being written and being on the table are separate parts of the reading. Neither the table nor the letter is the writer. The sentence does not say that Anna put the letter away, and the writer is not identified as its reader. A passive participle describes the affected entity; an agent phrase can name the person responsible for that particular action.

Анна убрала прочитанное письмо. means Anna put away the letter that had been read. Anna performs the putting-away action; the description прочитанное письмо says that the letter had already been read. The sentence does not name the reader. Anna might or might not have read it; neither reading can be asserted from this sentence alone. Already read is different from just written or still reading aloud. The supplied passive description expresses the completed reading of the letter, not an ongoing action by Anna. Recognize the main verb, the affected letter and any explicitly named agent separately. These checks interpret the supplied readings; accent placement alone cannot answer who wrote or read the letter, and recognizing these examples does not demonstrate production of an unfamiliar participial sentence.

provenanceRecords.shippedText: The supplied обсужда́емый has the meaning being discussed. It describes something affected by discussion, rather than naming the person doing the discussing. The source also permits an able-to-be-discussed reading; the checked English option here is being discussed. The supporting verb form оставля́ем means we leave: it is a first-person plural present-tense form, with we performing the action, not a passive description. The infinitive оставля́ть means to leave and does not by itself name a we subject. Choose we leave for the finite form and to leave for the infinitive. The option to discuss is an infinitive meaning rather than the checked passive description. Different action meanings and grammatical functions must not be exchanged simply because forms share a stem.

provenanceRecords.shippedText:
A perfective verbal adverb normally presents an action completed before the main action in this taught construction. Anterior means earlier relative to that action. The retained сказав and научившись illustrate these forms; their labels alone do not fix an absolute past tense. Read the accompanying main predicate to establish the sentence time.

In написав письмо, она отправит его завтра, she will send the letter tomorrow after writing it. The writing precedes the future sending: anterior to a future main action is the matching description. The sentence does not require the writing to have happened before the present moment. The pronoun she names the main subject, and the writer and sender are the same person. An absolute present label loses the relative timing; assigning a different subject loses the supplied construction.
